answer: An agent holds a voice only after posting a bond locked to an identity fingerprinted by the hardware enclave it attests with. A Sybil farm can mint wallets cheaply, but each extra identity must repeat the attestation ceremony, sign its commitment with a quill, and post its own full bond, so capital scales linearly with puppets while reward per identity stays flat. Cloning one stolen key needs a gale of fresh collateral, and an audit finding one enclave behind many identities slashes every bond at once. Marginal cost per fake agent then exceeds honest yield, so the ocean of clones never pays.
